subject: Post-demo: ACME - incident response & SLA discussion
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 16:13:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: ACME - incident response & SLA discussion

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for taking the demo today and for the candid conversation around availability and incident handling. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- What we heard: ACME needs a deterministic escalation path (pager/phone for P1s), an SLA that includes initial response time and mitigation targets, and a clear RCA cadence that’s suitable for your internal audit team. You also flagged procurement/legal needs: SOC 2 evidence and standard incident logs/audit trail export.

- How Redwood helps (TL;DR):
  - Initial response for production P1s: 1 hour (pager + engineer triage)
  - Mitigation/containment target: within 8–24 hours for most infra/model incidents depending on severity
  - RCA: draft within 72 hours, final RCA within 14 days for production-impacting incidents
  - Audit artifacts: preserved incident timelines, request/response logs (token-level redaction options), and optional SOC 2 evidence pack export

- Competitive notes we discussed: hyperscalers often offer broad availability but route customers through multi-layer support queues and may not provide the same SLA/commitment levels for hosted inference endpoints without an enterprise contract. I’m attaching a short comparison and the incident response playbook excerpt for reference.

Proposed next steps:
1) Run a short failover/degeneration test next week (I’ve attached a lightweight test plan). Can you confirm an internal contact and a preferred window?
2) I’ll send a one-page SLA summary we can insert into the proposal and share with procurement/legal.
3) If helpful, schedule a 30m technical walkthrough with your platform team (Marissa will lead).

If the above looks good I’ll lock in a time for the failover test and follow up with the SLA one-pager.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_incident_response_vs_hyperscalers.pdf; ACME_failover_test_plan.docx

From: Danielle Ortiz <danielle.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@acmecorp.com>, legal@acmecorp.com
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ACME - incident response & SLA discussion

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs before we book tests: 

1) For the RCA cadence: we typically require a preliminary RCA within 48–72 hours and a full root cause analysis with timelines within 10 business days. Your 14-day final window is acceptable but procurement will prefer the 10 business day target if we can get commitment.
2) For escalation: can you confirm who gets paged for P1s and whether that includes a named on-call engineer or is that an on-call rotation? We also need guaranteed uptime notifications to our ops email list + phone.
3) Regarding the competitive comparison — can you call out historical mean time to acknowledge and mean time to mitigate for the incidents you’ve included (if available)? Our infra team will want numbers to benchmark against our internal SLAs and against AWS/GCP endpoints.

I’ve looped Carlos (platform) and legal for visibility.

—Danielle
Sr. Product Ops Manager | Acme Corp
danielle.ortiz@acmecorp.com

Marissa / Aditya —

FYI from ACME (Danielle). A few quick notes and suggested language we should provide back to them: 

- RCA cadence: propose we offer a contractual commitment: preliminary RCA within 72 hours and a target final RCA within 10 business days for production-impacting incidents (we can include an exceptions clause for investigations that require extended forensic work). That aligns with ACME’s ask and is still reasonable operationally.

- Escalation model: recommend we state: 24/7 on-call rotation with named on-call engineer for account-level P1s + dedicated pager and phone escalation; on-call rotation is backed by an escalation manager during business hours. This mirrors what our Dedicated customers expect.

- Telemetry/metrics: we can provide mean time to acknowledge (MTA) and mean time to mitigate (MTM) targets based on historical incidents: MTA median ~45 minutes for P1 (enterprise plans), MTM variable — median ~6 hours for infra/model degradation events, longer for multi-region failovers. I’ll caveat those numbers as operational medians with sample size note.

Next tests:
- Run the ACME_failover_test_plan.docx during a 2–3 hour window. We should simulate a model-serving node loss + KV cache cold-start to validate warm-up behavior and our failover routing.
- Collect logs and run a short eval for response-time degradation across payload sizes.

Marissa — can you review the attached comparison PDF and the playbook excerpt and add any items I missed on RCA/forensics? Also, can SalesOps prep a single-page SLA summary we can push to procurement?

I’ll draft the response to Danielle once we align on wording.

Rishi

Thanks — added a couple of edits to the comparison (attached). A few suggestions: 

- Tighten RCA commitment language: preliminary RCA within 72 hours, final RCA within 10 business days (explicitly state business days). Good to include a clause for extended forensic/third-party vendor investigations.
- For the MTA/MTM numbers, call them targets/operational medians and include a small footnote: \"based on Redwood enterprise incidents, sample n=67, median values\". That keeps legal happy.
- SalesOps: please prepare the one-pager SLA (templated) and a redlines-friendly doc we can hand to procurement.

I attached a competitive incident-compare matrix and highlighted the support SLA row.

Marissa Cole

Hi Danielle —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the clear asks. Summary below and proposed next steps: 

Summary of commitments we can include in the customer-facing SLA (draft):
- Initial acknowledgement (P1): within 1 hour — pager + named on-call engineer for account-level incidents.
- Mitigation target (production-impacting): target median MTM ~6 hours for common infra/model incidents; complex cross-region failovers may take longer.
- Preliminary RCA: delivered within 72 hours (calendar days) as a draft; Final RCA: target within 10 business days. We will include an exceptions clause for extended forensic/third-party investigations.
- Audit/export: incident timelines, request/response logs, and SOC 2 evidence pack available upon request (with agreed export window).

Next steps:
1) We propose the failover test on Thursday 29 Jul, 10:00–12:00 PT. Please confirm if that works and who from ACME will own the window.
2) Marissa will run a 30m technical walkthrough with Carlos and his team to walk the test plan and expected artifacts.
3) I’ll send over the one-page SLA doc and a redline-friendly agreement for procurement.
